sheet: LaTeX is a markup-based typesetting system for structured documents.
A .tex file is source; a compiler produces PDF or another output format.
\section{} creates a section heading; \textbf{} makes text bold.
\frac{a}{b} creates a fraction; \sum and \int create mathematical operators.
Environments begin with \begin{name} and close with \end{name}.
Word processors use styles for consistent headings and document structure.
Automatic tables of contents use heading styles.
Track Changes records revisions; comments support review.
Citation tools manage references and bibliographies; check the required citation style.
PDF is a common fixed-layout output; retain editable source files.
tricks: Remember backslash commands and environment pairs.
Use heading styles before generating a contents page.
Check bibliography style and source completeness.
shortcuts: Start with documentclass and document environment.
Use inline math for symbols within a sentence.
Use display math for standalone equations.
Apply styles rather than manually formatting each heading.
remember: LaTeX source is not the PDF.

howto: Choose LaTeX when precise mathematical typesetting and reproducible source are important; choose a word processor when collaborative editing and familiar page-layout tools are central. Keep source files, apply semantic heading styles, and verify citations and final PDF output.

scenes.title: What is LaTeX?
body: LaTeX is a document preparation system built on TeX. Authors write structured source commands and compile the source into a typeset document.
A .tex file is editable source; PDF is a common compiled output.
LaTeX is particularly useful for mathematical notation, cross-references and consistent document structure.

items.ask: What is the difference between a .tex file and a PDF?
items.recall: The .tex file is source; PDF is a common compiled output.
refresh: A .tex file contains editable LaTeX commands and document content. A compiler processes this source to create a typeset output, commonly a PDF file.
Keep the source file when sharing a finished document. A PDF preserves layout for reading and printing, but it is not a replacement for the editable source used to revise and rebuild the document.

items.ask: What is an environment in LaTeX?
items.recall: A named region opened by begin and closed by end commands.
refresh: LaTeX environments group content with a particular structure or formatting rule. The usual pattern is a matching begin command and end command using the same environment name.

For example, the document environment contains the main document content. Other environments can format equations, tables, lists and other structured material; matching the opening and closing names is essential.

items.ask: Why use heading styles in a word processor?
items.recall: They provide consistent structure and support navigation and automatic contents.
refresh: Heading styles apply a consistent visual treatment and a semantic level to each heading. This makes a long report easier to navigate and helps keep the hierarchy consistent when sections are moved or revised.

Automatic tables of contents can be generated from those heading levels and updated after edits. Manually enlarging and bolding text may look similar, but it does not reliably provide the same document structure.

scenes.title: A document has a structure
body: A minimal LaTeX document declares a class, begins the document environment, contains content and ends the document environment.
The preamble appears before begin{document} and commonly contains packages and configuration.

scenario.title: A scholar creates an equation-rich note
body: A scholar needs a document with numbered sections, equations and references. A LaTeX source file provides a reproducible structure and can be compiled to PDF.
The document class controls the overall document type and layout.

The scholar should keep the editable source, bibliography data and any required supporting files together with the final output. Before submission, the document should be compiled or exported again after the last revision, and the headings, equation layout, page numbers, cross-references and bibliography should be checked in the final reading copy.

scenes.title: Mathematics: inline and displayed

blocks.body: Use inline math delimiters for a mathematical expression within a sentence.
Use display math delimiters or a suitable equation environment for a standalone equation.
frac creates a fraction; sum creates a summation symbol; int creates an integral symbol.

ask.q: Which delimiters are used for inline mathematics?

body: Use \( ... \) for a mathematical expression within a sentence.
Use \[ ... \] or a suitable equation environment for a standalone equation.
\frac{a}{b} creates a fraction; \sum creates a summation symbol; \int creates an integral symbol.

scenes.title: Choose the right math mode
scenes.problem: A sentence contains the symbol beta, followed by a standalone equation for the sample mean. Which math modes are appropriate?
hints: A symbol embedded in a sentence is inline.
A standalone equation should be displayed.
scenes.answer: Use \(\beta\) inline and \[\bar{x}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\] as display mathematics.
scenes.check: Inline and display modes serve different layout purposes.

solution.why: Inline delimiters keep the symbol within the paragraph's text flow.

solution.say: Use display delimiters \[ ... \] for the sample-mean equation.
solution.why: Display delimiters place the equation on its own line.

solution.say: Match the delimiter to the layout.
solution.math: Inline mathematics stays in the paragraph; display mathematics is set apart.
solution.why: The two forms differ in how mathematics is placed relative to surrounding text.

scenes.title: Word processors and document structure

blocks.body: Heading styles apply consistent formatting and semantic structure to headings.
A table of contents can be generated from heading styles and updated when headings or page numbers change.
Headers, footers, page numbers, margins, section breaks and tables support long-form documents.

ask.q: Why use heading styles instead of manually enlarging every heading?
ask.nudge: Styles keep formatting consistent and support automatic navigation.

scenes.title: Review and reference a document
scenes.problem: A supervisor reviews a draft and requests tracked edits, comments and a consistent bibliography. Name the appropriate features.
hints: Use a revision-tracking feature for edits.
Use a citation manager or built-in references tool for bibliography management.
scenes.answer: Track Changes, comments, and a citation/reference manager.
scenes.check: Each feature supports a distinct part of collaborative document preparation.

scenario.title: A supervisor and scholar collaborate
body: A supervisor needs to see edits, leave review notes and ensure references are consistently formatted. Track Changes records modifications; comments capture feedback; citation tools manage source metadata and bibliography output.

The scholar should keep the editable source, bibliography data and any required supporting files together with the final output. Before submission, the document should be compiled or exported again after the last revision, and the headings, equation layout, page numbers, cross-references and bibliography should be checked in the final reading copy.
scenario.q: Which feature records edits made to the document?

ask.q: What is the purpose of a citation manager?
ask.nudge: It organises references and bibliography data.

solution.say: Record edits made by the reviewer.
solution.why: Track Changes records insertions, deletions and revisions for review.

solution.say: Attach review feedback to the draft.
solution.why: Comments let reviewers explain or discuss particular passages without rewriting the document body.

solution.say: Keep citations and the bibliography consistent.
solution.why: A reference manager stores bibliographic metadata and helps format in-text citations and the reference list.
